title: Suicide Island
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: After repeated suicide attempts, Sei is declared legally dead and exiled to a remote island with other suicide survivors, where there are no rules except that escape is forbidden. After seeing the brutal results of suicide attempts there, Sei and others decide that if they cannot die they must learn to live: hunting, fishing, building shelter and community, while other groups descend into violence (Wikipedia; Dark Horse).
life_message: Life is worth choosing: purpose comes from hard work, mutual care and the daily labor of staying alive together.

content.note: Rival groups turn violent (Wikipedia); hunting and killing animals, cannibalism listed (MU); compared to Battle Royale (Dark Horse).
Characters 'barely holding onto sanity' (Dark Horse); tragedy and survival (AniList).
MU lists Rape, Attempted Rape, Child Rape; AniList Rape 60 (spoiler). Capped at 3 pending a non-database source (to verify); likely understated.
Suicide and attempts are the premise (Wikipedia; Dark Horse 18+; AniList Suicide 92; MU Depression).
Suicide attempts depicted with brutal consequences (Wikipedia); also practical survival skills (AniList Educational).

dominant: choosing to live; building community from nothing; survival in nature; critique of a society that abandons the suicidal

frames.aligns: Life chosen as worth living; mutual aid among the despairing.
frames.concerns: Graphic suicide attempts and sexual violence (MU).

Dignity vs honor.evidence: No courts, yet Sei's group builds rules rather than feuds (Wikipedia).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Lawless island; group creates its own order (Wikipedia).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Strangers form a community, not a clan (Wikipedia).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Practical skills of hunting, fishing, archery (AniList, MU).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Food, shelter and survival dominate (Wikipedia; AniList Survival).

folkways.japan: Japan's high public concern over suicide and social isolation frames the premise of a state that writes off suicidal citizens, described here as context.

delivery.evidence: Wikipedia shows the 'learn to live' choice made in plot; no review of tone opened (to verify).

personified.ideology: If we cannot die, we must learn to live

delivery.note: The pro-life choice is carried by survival work and community-building.

winners_losers: Sei's cooperative group gains a reason to live; groups that turn to violence are shown spiraling. Sympathy goes to community and labor.
